# Quick Summary — Unit 6: Animal Tissue
### Persona: Intermediate | D_target: 5 | Word Count: ~918

---

## 1. History & Overview

- **Xavier Bichat** coined 'tissue'; **Father + Founder** of animal histology; **21 types** without microscope.
- **Karl Mayer** coined 'histology' **(1801)**; **Marcello Malpighi** = Founder of histology.
- **Phylum Coelenterata** = first phylum with tissue-grade organization; all 4 tissues first in **Platyhelminthes**.
- Animal tissue definition: group of cells with common **origin**; structure, location, function may differ; cells secrete **matrix** (CT has cells + matrix + fibres; ET/MT/NT have cells + matrix only).

## 2. Epithelial Tissue

- **Avascular**; **basement membrane** = white collagen; origin from all **3 germ layers**.
- **Cell junctions**: Tight (zonula occludens), Adherens (zonula adherens), Desmosome (macula adherens), Gap (septate junction).

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Chapter-level: Animal Tissue and Histology Foundations" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

### Simple Epithelium (4 types)

- **Simple Squamous**: Endothelium (endoderm — capillary, endocardium, tunica interna); Mesothelium (mesoderm — parietal, visceral/splanchnic).
- **Simple Cuboidal**: Brush-bordered = **PCT of nephrons** (selective reabsorption).
- **Simple Columnar**: Brush-bordered = **intestinal mucosa** (absorption); Ciliated = fallopian tube, oviduct, neurocoel.
- **Pseudostratified**: single layer but appears multilayered; **ciliated** + **goblet cells**; in upper respiratory tract, trachea, bronchi — for air filtration.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Overview of all historians + tissue grade hierarchy" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

### Compound Epithelium

- **Stratified squamous**: Non-keratinized (buccal cavity, oesophagus, vagina — keeps moist); Keratinized (skin + derivatives — waterproof, protection).
- **Stratified cuboidal**: Rare — ducts of salivary/sweat/mammary glands.
- **Stratified columnar**: Uncommon — conjunctiva, pharynx, male urethra.
- **Transitional = Urothelium = Plastic epithelium**: bears stress; cells change shape (rounded → flattened when stretched); renal pelvis, ureter, urinary bladder, urethra.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Marcello Malpighi: Founder of histology" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

### Modified Epithelium

- **Kino-ciliated**: **9+2** microtubule arrangement (9 peripheral doublets + 2 central singlets) — in respiratory organs, female reproductive tract, neurocoel.
- **Stereo-ciliated**: **0+0** (no microtubules) — in epididymis (sperm maturation + storage).
- **Brush-bordered**: microvilli on free border — kidney tubules + small intestine (↑ absorptive surface).
- **Glandular ET**: By Ducts: Exocrine (ducted/enzymes), Endocrine (ductless/hormones), Heterocrine/Mixed (e.g., pancreas); By Secretion Quantity: Apocrine (mammary), Merocrine (salivary), Holocrine (sebaceous).

## 3. Connective Tissue

- **CT cells**: Fibroblasts (principal), Mast cells (modified basophils — heparin/histamine/serotonin — proper CT only), Histocytes (modified monocytes — macrophage — proper CT only), Lymphocytes (antibodies), Plasma cells (cartwheel cells — modified lymphocytes — antibodies/immunoglobulins).
- **CT fibres**: Collagen = White (inelastic, bundled); Elastic = Yellow (branched, elastic); Reticulate = Colourless (forms stroma).
- **Areolar tissue** = packing tissue (beneath skin); **Adipose** = modified areolar with adipocytes — White (abdomen, hump, blubber) + Brown (migratory birds, hibernating rats, newborns).
- **Dense CT**: White fibrous (skull sutures — immovable); Tendon (muscle→bone); Ligament (bone→bone, has some elastic fibres).
- **Cartilage**: avascular; chondrocytes in lacunae; 4 types: Hyaline (most abundant, gristle), Calcified (coated CaCO₃), Fibrocartilage (strongest, white fibrous, no perichondrium), Elastic (yellow fibrous, pinna, larynx).
- **Bone**: vascular; osteocytes; ossein matrix; 65% inorganic + 15% organic + 10% water.

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="The Epithelial Basement Membrane" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

**Blood Cell Hierarchy:**

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="General features combined overview" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Blood Cells 45%]
  A --> B[RBCs - Erythrocytes]
  A --> C[WBCs - Leucocytes]
  A --> D[Platelets - Thrombocytes]
  C --> E[Granulocytes]
  C --> F[Agranulocytes]
  E --> G[Neutrophils 60-70%]
  E --> H[Basophils 0.5-1%]
  E --> I[Eosinophils 2-4%]
  F --> J[Lymphocytes 20-25%]
  F --> K[Monocytes 3-8%]
```

<img src="data:image/jpeg;base64," alt="Avascular survival and diffusion-based nutrition" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; border-radius: 8px; margin: 12px 0;" />

- **Plasma** = 55%: 90% water + 7% proteins (albumins — osmotic pressure; globulins — transport + immunity) + 3% others.
- **RBC**: Mammalian — biconcave, non-nucleated, anaerobic respiration; lifespan = **120 days**; count = 5 million mm⁻³ (male).
- **WBC**: RBC:WBC = **600:1**; lifespan = 12–20 days. Neutrophils = most abundant (60–70%); Basophils = least (0.5–1%).
- **Platelets/Thrombocytes**: 0.15–0.4 million mm⁻³; lifespan 7–10 days; releases thromboplastin for blood clotting.

## 4. Muscular Tissue

- **Skeletal/Striped**: voluntary; syncytial (multinucleated); **Red** (myoglobin — man, goat) vs **White** (no myoglobin — athletes, fish); Sliding filament theory = **Huxley and Hanson**.
- **Smooth/Unstriped**: involuntary; spindle-shaped, uninucleated; **Single-unit** (urinary bladder, alimentary canal) vs **Multi-unit** (arrector pilli, blood vessels).
- **Cardiac**: involuntary, never fatigues; separated by **intercalated discs**; single nucleus per cardiocyte; faint transverse striations.
- Coverings: myofibre = **endomysium**; fascicle = **perimysium**; block = **epimysium**.

## 5. Nervous Tissue

- **CNS Neuroglia** (4 types): Astrocyte (star-shaped, regulates neuro-environment), Oligodendrocyte (forms myelin sheath in CNS), Microglia (macrophage — mesodermal), Ependymal cell (lines ventricles, secretes CSF).
- **PNS Neuroglia** (2 types): Stellate cell (surrounds soma), Schwann cell (forms myelin sheath in PNS, heals injury).
- **Neurone = Soma + Neurites**: Soma (Cyton) has Nissl's granules (RNA + ribosomes + RER); Dendrite = afferent; Axon = efferent (single, unbranched).
- **Axon**: covered by oligodendrocytes (CNS) or Schwann cells (PNS); myelin sheath (phospholipids) = white/fast; **Nodes of Ranvier** = unmyelinated gaps; saltatory conduction.
- **By direction**: Sensory (Afferent), Motor (Efferent), Intermediate (Adjustor).
- **Gray matter** = outer brain + inner spinal cord; **White matter** = inner brain + outer spinal cord.
